name: tmux
one_line: terminal multiplexer: many terminals in one, that survive disconnects
plain: `tmux` lets you run several terminal windows and split panes inside one terminal, and keeps them running if your connection drops. You can leave a long scan or a shell running, close the window, and come back later with the session intact.

All its keyboard commands start with a prefix key, Ctrl+B (hold Ctrl, press B, release, then press the next key). For a CTF it means: one pane for the exploit, one for the listener, one for notes, all at once, and a lifeline over SSH.
when: Run several things side by side in one window.
Keep a long job running after you disconnect from SSH.
Share a terminal layout between sessions.
Scroll back through output and copy text.

examples.title: Start a named session
examples.explain: Creates a session called ctf. You are now inside it.

examples.title: Leave it running and come back
examples.cmd:
Ctrl+B then D     (detach)
tmux attach -t ctf
examples.explain: Detach leaves everything running; attach reconnects.

examples.title: Split the window
examples.cmd:
Ctrl+B then %    (side by side)
Ctrl+B then "    (one above the other)
examples.explain: Panes let you watch a listener while you type in another.

examples.title: Move between panes
examples.cmd: Ctrl+B then arrow keys   or   Ctrl+B then O
examples.explain: Arrow keys jump to the pane in that direction.

examples.title: New window and switching
examples.cmd: Ctrl+B then C (new)   N (next)   P (previous)   0-9 (go to)
examples.explain: Windows are like tabs inside the session.

examples.title: Scroll and copy
examples.cmd: Ctrl+B then [   (copy mode), arrows or PgUp, Q to leave
examples.explain: Copy mode lets you scroll back; Space starts a selection and Enter copies it (in default emacs keys).

examples.title: Zoom one pane
examples.explain: Makes the current pane fill the window; press again to return.

examples.title: Kill a session
examples.explain: Ends a session and everything in it.

mistakes: Forgetting the prefix and typing the command key directly into the shell.
Nesting tmux inside tmux (over SSH) and sending the prefix to the wrong one: press the prefix twice.
Closing the terminal with exit instead of detaching: exit inside the shell ends the pane.
Not using named sessions and losing track of them.
Copying text with the mouse and wondering why it is not in the clipboard: use copy mode or enable mouse support.
try: Start a session, split into three panes, run top, a listener and a shell.
Open ~/.tmux.conf, turn on mouse mode and reload with tmux source-file ~/.tmux.conf.
